subject: Nebula Health — dedicated GPU headroom, fallthrough & slotting plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Nebula Health — incoming dedicated sizing request (headroom + fallthrough)

Team,

Quick inbound from Sara at Nebula Health (attached perf CSV). Key asks: predictable dedicated capacity for clinical-chat and batch-embedding workloads, 99th latency SLO of 1.5s for chat, cost target that is ~25% below their current provider. Workload summary (from customer):
- Peak concurrent active chats: ~110 sessions (mix of short synchronous QA and longer note-generation flows)
- Avg tokens generated per response: 900 tokens
- Embedding throughput: average 1k small-batch requests/min, burst to 3k/min
- Model mix: a small high-quality 70B variant for clinician-facing responses (rare long-context sessions), primary 13B/33B family for most production traffic, and an embedding model family.

Questions we need answered for the proposal:
1) Recommended primary SKU(s) for the Dedicated pool (H100 / A100 / L4) balancing memory needs for the 70B variant vs cost for the bulk 13/33B and embeddings.
2) Suggested headroom reserve (percent) for autoscale + cold-starts and a fallthrough/fallback policy to keep them within SLA if capacity hits limits.
3) Operational notes: preferred KV/prefix caching sizing, recommended model-variant pinning strategy, and whether a hybrid mix (e.g., A100 + L4) is appropriate.

I attached their perf dump (nebula_perf_summary.csv) and will draft the external proposal once we have a sizing recommendation.

Thanks,
Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Nebula Health — incoming dedicated sizing request (headroom + fallthrough)

Vivek / all,

Thanks for the data — dug through the CSV and their token distribution looks spiky (short chats are common, but ~10% of sessions go long). High-level recommendation: a hybrid pool with A100 primary and L4 burst/embedding tiers, with H100 reserved only for scheduled long-context runs or an opt-in premium queue. Rationale below.

Summary recommendation (quick):
- Primary pool: A100 40GB (mixed-precision / 4-bit quantized for 13B/33B). Use A100 as the baseline because it balances memory (40GB) for mid-sized models and better throughput for generation-heavy sessions compared to L4.
- Embedding/burst tier: L4 instances (cost-efficient, high-density for small-context embedding serving). Route stateless embedding and low-context chat to L4.
- H100: Provision a small reserved H100 80GB capacity (3–4 cards) for the 70B long-context variant and for predictable low-latency premium paths. Do not make H100 the primary — cost per GPU and utilization risk are high.

Sizing calc (back-of-envelope):
- Customer target peak concurrent sessions: 110 active
- Average generation time tokens: 900 tokens/response. At ~200 tokens/sec effective model throughput (13B quantized on A100), that's ~4.5s per request on average if run single-threaded. With batching and continuous-mode we can push effective throughput to ~600 tokens/sec per GPU for generation-heavy flows.
- Conservative per-GPU concurrent sessions (A100): ~12 concurrent small-medium sessions (with batching + prefix cache). That suggests ~10 A100 GPUs to support steady-state 110 sessions with ~20% headroom => 12 GPUs.
- Embedding capacity (L4): estimate 2 L4s to handle baseline embedding QPS with room for 2x bursts.
- H100: 3 cards for scheduled/priority 70B runs and for emergency fallback.

Headroom + fallthrough:
- Recommend 20% reserved headroom on the committed pool for autoscale trigger (immediately available burst via Dedicated burst capacity).
- Fallthrough policy: if A100 pool saturated, route low-priority or older-model requests to L4 with degraded latency but maintained success — for premium clinician flows route to H100 (if available) or return a soft-error with automatic retry/backoff.

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix cache: allocate 30% of aggregate memory across the pool for KV caching (reduces token compute for repeated contexts). Suggest a dedicated cache node group (can be L4-backed) to avoid eviction pressure on generation GPUs.
- Model pinning: pin their 70B variant to the H100 reserved pool; pin 13B/33B to A100. Allow dynamic routing rules in the config so we can change thresholds without redeploy.
- Quantization guidance: encourage 4-bit quant for 13/33B on A100; do not quantize the 70B until we validate quality.

Risks / notes:
- Cost sensitivity: A100 primary + H100 reserve is larger TCO than pure L4. If Nebula's budget is tight, we can trade 1–2 A100s for additional L4s, but expect higher tail latency on generation-heavy sessions and potentially lower throughput for 33B models.
- We should explicitly call out expected P95/P99 latency tradeoffs in the proposal.

I'll draft numbers into a simple quote sheet (attaching a sample). If this looks good I can convert into the external proposal PDF for the customer.

- Marissa

Attachment: nebula_perf_summary.csv (referenced), draft-quote.xlsx (internal)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara@nebula.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:14:00 +0000
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated capacity plan (A100 primary + L4 burst; reserved H100 for long-context)

Sara,

Thanks for the perf data and the time earlier. Per our internal sizing call (summary below and attached PDF), we recommend the following Dedicated configuration to meet your latency targets while optimizing cost:

- Primary pool: 12 x A100 40GB (handles majority of 13B/33B production traffic; supports quantized inference and steady batching)
- Burst/embedding tier: 2 x L4 (stateless, cost-efficient for embeddings and small-context chat)
- Reserved H100 pool: 3 x H100 80GB (pinned for 70B long-context runs and premium clinician queue)
- Headroom: 20% reserved for autoscale and short bursts; additional burst capacity available on request.

Operational highlights:
- KV/prefix cache configured with dedicated cache nodes to reduce repeated-token compute; we propose reserving ~30% aggregate memory for cache footprint.
- Routing: requests are routed by policy (model, latency priority, cost envelope). If A100 pool is saturated low-priority flows fall back to L4; premium flows fall back to H100 if available.
- Timeline: 2–3 weeks for Dedicated provisioning once PO and SOC paperwork are in place.

I've attached a formal quote (nb-proposal-dedicated-capacity-quote.pdf) and the perf summary you provided. Next steps: confirm the SLO targets (P95/P99), confirm acceptance of hybrid SKU mix, and sign the PO so we can secure the H100 reservation.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks for the fast turn. We reviewed the proposal with ops and engineering. A few quick items before we sign:

1) Budget: Our procurement team asked if you can show a cost sensitivity where we replace 2 A100s with 6–8 additional L4s to lower monthly committed spend. We understand throughput will be lower for 33B models, but want a clear expected delta in P95/P99 and cost.
2) Compliance: We need SOC2 evidence and a short note on how audit logs for Dedicated are exposed (log retention window). Can you attach the SOC2 summary and a sample audit log export?
3) Private deployment: ops asked about the timeline and feasibility for a VPC-private control plane (we may prefer private for PHI). If Private adds >3 weeks we need a plan to start with Hosted/Dedicated and migrate later.

If you can get those three items back to us this week we can route for fast approval.

— Sara
